security_audit.summary: All 96 static findings are false positives because the only scanned file is security guidance containing illustrative code and prevention examples. No executable implementation, prompt injection, or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Security examples trigger pattern-based scanners when their unsafe forms appear in explanatory code blocks.
remediation.suggestion: Keep unsafe examples clearly labeled and consider scanner-aware annotations or separate documentation fixtures so marketplace scanning can distinguish guidance from executable code.

remediation.issue: The skill references external security checklist material using relative paths.
remediation.suggestion: Publish and validate the referenced checklist with the skill, or document the required repository layout so users do not lose important guidance.

content.value_statement: Security weaknesses often enter through untrusted input, weak authorization, exposed secrets, and unsafe integrations. This skill provides practical controls and review checklists to reduce those risks before release.
actual_capabilities: Map trust boundaries and assets with a concise STRIDE threat model.
Recommend validation, authorization, session, security-header, and rate-limiting controls.
Identify unsafe SQL, HTML, URL-fetch, filesystem, and LLM-output handling patterns.
Guide dependency audit triage, lockfile governance, and install-script review.
Define secret-management, privacy, retention, consent, export, and deletion practices.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not modify or execute application code.
It cannot prove that a control is correctly implemented without access to the complete application and deployment environment.
It does not replace penetration testing, dependency intelligence, legal advice, or incident response.
Recommendations require adaptation to the framework, hosting platform, data types, and threat model.

use_cases.title: Review an API Endpoint
use_cases.description: Map inputs and assets, then check validation, authorization, query handling, error responses, rate limits, and logging.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Secure Release
use_cases.description: Triage dependency advisories, verify the lockfile and package manager, review install scripts, and check secret handling.

use_cases.title: Assess Privacy Controls
use_cases.description: Classify personal data, define purpose and retention, and plan consent, export, deletion, and third-party sharing controls.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature description for trust boundaries, sensitive assets, untrusted inputs, and likely abuse cases. List the highest-priority risks.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this API endpoint design. Recommend concrete controls for validation, authentication, authorization, SQL, XSS, SSRF, errors, rate limits, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Dependency Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these package audit results by severity, reachability, runtime exposure, available fixes, lockfile integrity, and installation-script risk. Provide an ordered remediation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review an LLM Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat-model this LLM workflow. Check prompt injection, output handling, secret exposure, tenant isolation, tool permissions, destructive actions, and consumption limits. Propose tests and code-level safeguards.

output_examples.input: A webhook endpoint accepts a URL and fetches it on the server.
output: Risk: server-side request forgery can reach internal services or cloud metadata.
Control: allow only approved HTTPS hosts, resolve all addresses, reject private ranges, and disable redirects.
Test: verify blocked localhost, private IP, metadata, redirect, and DNS-rebinding cases.

output_examples.input: A team wants to store login tokens in browser storage.
output_examples.output: Use secure, httpOnly, sameSite cookies for sessions. Add expiration, rotation, CSRF defenses, and server-side authorization checks.

output_examples.input: An application sends customer records to an analytics or LLM vendor.
output: Classify the fields and remove data that is not required.
Obtain and record appropriate consent before sharing.
Confirm contractual, retention, residency, access, and deletion controls with the vendor.

best_practices: Validate and authorize data at every trust boundary, including model output and internal service messages.
Keep secrets out of source, logs, prompts, responses, and client-accessible storage.
Turn security guidance into abuse-case tests and verify controls in the target deployment.
anti_patterns: Treating authentication as authorization or relying on client-side validation.
Passing untrusted or model-generated text into SQL, shells, eval, HTML, or filesystem paths.
Collecting personal data without a stated purpose, retention limit, consent path, or deletion workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews application design and implementation guidance across input handling, authentication, authorization, data protection, integrations, dependencies, privacy, and AI features.

faq.question: Does it run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured review process and recommendations. Use dedicated scanners and package-manager audits for automated detection.

faq.question: Can it secure an existing application?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant architecture, code, configuration, deployment context, and known findings for a prioritized review.

faq.question: Does it replace penetration testing?
faq.answer: No. It supports secure design and code review, but penetration testing is still needed for suitable applications and threat models.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It recommends environment-based secret management, strict repository exclusions, limited exposure, rotation after compromise, and no sensitive logging.

faq.question: Can it review LLM applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses prompt injection, untrusted model output, excessive agency, secret exposure, retrieval isolation, and resource consumption.
